subject: Renewal: term swap + usage floor proposal for ForgeWay
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@forgeway.ai>, Tom Blake <t.blake@forgeway.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: term swap + usage floor proposal for ForgeWay

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I pulled together a focused proposal that aims to: keep your unit economics predictable through next year, give you burst capacity for Q4, and protect ForgeWay from near-term price movement while you ramp new product traffic. Attached is a short workbook with line-items and an example monthly true-up cadence (FW_Renewal_Workbook.xlsx).

Key points up front:
- Term: move from 12mo to an 18mo term (start date 2027-07-01) to smooth pricing and avoid churn-related step-ups.
- Commit: 1.2M tokens/month committed baseline (10% uplift vs current run-rate) with a quarterly true-up.
- Bridging credits: $40k (applied as usage credits over first 3 months to absorb onboarding spikes).
- Price hold: Redwood will hold current per-token rate for the first 6 months of the renewed term.
- Overage: capped at 1.25x list after commit is exhausted; we can bake in an automatic burst pool to avoid sudden throttles.

Next steps I suggest: internal alignment from your finance team on the sign-by date (we've penciled 2027-06-30), and legal review of the attached redlines. Happy to jump on a 30-min call Thurs to run the numbers with Priyom if helpful.

Best,
Marcus

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal: term swap + usage floor proposal for ForgeWay

Marcus — quick read through and a couple of engineering/ops notes before you send to legal: 

1) Burst capacity: we can guarantee a 2x short-term burst pool for 14 days if we add a small reserved buffer. That maps to the workbook's "burst credit" row; figure in ~0.8 GPU-hours/day peak for their expected pattern.
2) Commit split suggestion: consider a two-tier commit (base + variable guaranteed). Example: 900k tokens/month base + 300k tokens/month guaranteed variable that converts to base if not reduced after 6 months. That helps protect the customer if they overcommit up-front.
3) Price hold implementation: we need a clause that defines the price hold window (6 months) and a rollback trigger (e.g., if underlying HW costs change >12%). Legal loves explicit triggers.

I've dropped a marked-up copy of the contract into the shared drive and attached the current legal redlines (legal_markups_v3.pdf). If you want I can join the call Thurs to walk the tech constraints.

— Priyom
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Samira Khan <samira@forgeway.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: term swap + usage floor proposal for ForgeWay

Marcus,

Thanks for the proposal and the workbook — this is close to what Finance expected. A few items we need clarified before we can move to legal: 

- Minimum commit: we need the baseline to be 800k tokens/month (our forecast shows uneven ramp and Finance won't approve 1.2M baseline). Can you run the numbers with 800k baseline + ability to true-up monthly?
- Price hold duration: we require a 6-month hold from sign date (we can accept triggers tied to public cloud GPU pricing but need a cap on pass-through increases).
- Credits: the $40k bridging credit is appreciated. Can we structure it as an "onboarding consumption credit" that applies only to base/variable usage (not overages)?
- Procurement: our procurement team requests a separate signature flow (DocuSign + PO). We also need SOC 2 Type II evidence and the latest security questionnaire filled; can you route that to our security contact (cc'ed Tom Blake)

If you can send an updated, clean summary with the revised baseline and how credits apply (line-by-line) we'll share with procurement. We aim to sign by 2027-06-30 if numbers align.

Cheers,
Samira Khan
VP of Platform, ForgeWay
samira@forgeway.ai

Samira / Tom —

Appreciate the quick review and the procurement/controls notes. Per Priyom's feasibility comments, here's an explicit, updated summary you can forward to procurement and legal: 

Executive summary (updated)
- Term: 18 months; term start 2027-07-01; early termination language unchanged.
- Commit: 800k tokens/month base (customer-requested). Variable guaranteed bucket: 400k tokens/month for Q1 (will convert to base at the 6-month mark unless ForgeWay elects otherwise). Net committed baseline in month 1 = 1.2M tokens available, billed as 800k base + 400k guaranteed variable.
- Bridging credits: $40,000 onboarding consumption credit. Applied first to base/variable usage only; not applied to overages or third-party services. Credits amortized over month 1-3 and shown line-by-line in the attached workbook.
- Price hold: 6 months from sign date. Any upstream infra cost increase >12% triggers a capped adjustment; cap set to +6% for the remainder of the hold period.
- Overage: capped at 1.25x list rate; Redwood will enable an automatic burst pool to smooth spikes.
- Approval & procurement flow: we will accept DocuSign + PO as you requested. I attached a clean "sign-ready" summary (embedded as the first sheet in the workbook) and included links below to HubSpot deal and DocuSign.

Action items and timeline
- Today: Marcus to upload the sign-ready workbook and send to procurement (done).
- 2027-06-10: Procurement to confirm PO path and send SOC 2 contact for questionnaire.
- 2027-06-24: Final contract returned with DocuSign link.
- 2027-06-30: Target sign date.

If this aligns I'll route a final playbook to legal with the system-level triggers and join your procurement call. Priyom — if you're comfortable with the variable-to-base conversion language above, please confirm and I'll include your line-item in the SOW. Lauren — looping you for any commercial approvals on the credit amortization schedule.

Thanks — talk soon.
Marcus
